plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY10 creating texts for purpose and audience; VC2E5LY12 writing legibly, fluently and automatically; VC2E5LY11 final editing against agreed criteria
plan.shape: check, title, publish, share: a last check against the checklist, a title that hooks, a clean final copy, then sharing with a real audience and reflecting on growth
plan.criticalFeature: a published piece is clean, clear and written for its reader, so nothing gets in the way of the message
decisionPoints: the choice check: the publish-ready paragraph
the exit board: a new sentence made publish-ready
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Today the whole piece goes out into the world.
plan.catchUp: No finished draft? Publish the strongest paragraphs you have, with a title and your best handwriting.

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: today your writing goes out into the world.

Print two Final Copy Pages per student, the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. Book the audience: another class, the newsletter or a real organisation. Collect the final copies for a class collection, Voices for the Arctic.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to publish a polished persuasive piece for a real audience.
successCriteria: I can do a final check of my writing.
I can publish a clean, clear final copy for my reader.
I can reflect on how my writing has grown.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Five weeks of thinking, arguing and drafting. Today it goes public.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: Who will read your writing?
lines: What do they need from a published piece?

notes.answer: neat, correct, a clear title, easy to read, convincing
beats: SAY: Fill in today's audience on the board.
Real people will read your writing.
ASK: What will your readers need from a published piece?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: neat writing, no mistakes, a good title, clear paragraphs
ASK: How ready do you feel to publish?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: mostly up or sideways
SAY: Check, title, final copy, share. Let's go.
trap: thinking publish means copying it out again, unchanged.
Fix: say publishing is the last chance to fix and polish.
notes.prep: Name the real audience before the session; it is the strongest motivation on Publish Day. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: To share a finished piece with a real audience.

notes.answer: to share a finished piece with a real audience
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Publish. Say it with me. Publish.
SAY: To share a finished piece with a real audience.
SAY: Our class collection is published for families to read.
ASK: Who could we publish our writing for?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: families, another class, the council, the newsletter
trap: thinking publish only means a printed book.
Fix: say a newsletter, a website or reading aloud are publishing too.
notes.prep: The word sets up the audience for the share at the end.

rows: short, hooking, centred at the top
a new line for each, with space between
your best: joined, even, on the lines
By: your name. Written for: your reader.

notes.answer: title, paragraphs, best handwriting, every fix copied, signed
beats: POINT to Title.
SAY: The title is the first thing your reader sees. Make it hook.
POINT to Paragraphs.
SAY: Each paragraph on a new line, with a gap. Readers need to see your structure.
POINT to Checked.
SAY: Copy every fix across. A final copy with old mistakes in it isn't final.
ASK: Which row will you need to watch most carefully?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: handwriting; copying fixes across
trap: copying from the old draft and missing the coloured fixes.
Fix: student ticks each fix as it is copied.
notes.stretch: Add a short author's line under your title.
notes.help: Copy one paragraph at a time, ticking each fix.
notes.prep: The model. VC2E5LY12: legible, fluent final copy. Typed copies are fine where the school allows.

slides.title: Ready or not?
slides.pivot: check each against the publish-ready table
slides.followUp: cold call one student: what would make it ready?

items.text: Every paragraph starts on a new line with a gap.
The last line says: Please switch off one light tonight.
items.answer: 1 - ready: a clear call to action

items.text: The draft's coloured fixes weren't copied into the final copy.
items.answer: 2 - not ready: copy the fixes across

items.text: It says: Written for: the zoo director.
Paragraph 2 is squeezed into the margin.
items.answer: 2 - not ready: start it on a new line

say: One finger ready, two not ready yet.
trap: voting ready because it sounds fine.
Fix: check against the table, row by row.
notes.stretch: Fix each one that isn't ready.
notes.help: Look at the table on the slide before.
notes.prep: Guided check before the final copy. SC1.

options.text: Polar bears need our help. According to NASA, the ice is shrinking.
Polar bears need our help!!!!! The ice is shrinking!!!!!
options.misconception: thinks lots of punctuation is polish; lost the source

notes.answer: B - capitals, comma, spelling and the source all right
beats: SAY: Three final copies of the same paragraph. Only one is ready.
ASK: Which paragraph is publish-ready?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: what went wrong in C?
Less -> run CUPS on each together, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. Every fix is there, and nothing distracts the reader.
trap: pointing to C because it looks excited.
Fix: ask where did the proof go? Student sees it is missing.
notes.prep: Decision point before the final copy. Under 80% means everyone runs the Worksheet's check row by row before copying.

slides.title: Publish your piece
slides.task: Do the final check and title on your Worksheet. Then write your final copy on the Final Copy Page, in your best handwriting.

notes.answer: a clean, titled, signed final copy
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Final check first. Then your best handwriting, one paragraph at a time.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Spot check: is that fix from the draft copied across?
ASK: How many paragraphs are on your final copy?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 2 or 3 by halfway
trap: rushing the final copy and adding new mistakes.
Fix: student reads each finished paragraph aloud before starting the next.
notes.stretch: Extension: an author's note and a blurb for the class collection.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: a picture checklist and frames; publish the best paragraphs.
notes.prep: Independent publishing, about 25 minutes. Leave 8 minutes for the share. SC2.

slides.extendedTask: a final check and title, then the published final copy

slides.title: Share it: gallery walk
lines: Lay your final copy on your desk.
Read three pieces. Leave a sticky note on each:

notes.answer: open - notes say what the reader wants to do
beats: SAY: Real readers react. Your note tells the writer their piece worked.
CIRCULATE with the class. Read notes aloud that name an action.
ASK: Point to a piece that made you want to act.
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to it... now.
EXPECT: a few pieces get many points
ASK: What did that writer do to persuade you?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: their story made me care; their fact surprised me
trap: Fix: model one: This made me want to switch off lights.
notes.prep: The authentic-audience share. If another class visits, they write the sticky notes. 8 minutes. SC3.
